sources.title: The Nazca Lines
sources.author: Nazca Civilization
sources.excerpt: Hummingbirds, spiders, monkeys, and geometric patterns stretch across the desert, visible only from the sky.
sources.longExcerpt: Across the Nazca desert, lines run straight for kilometers, triangles and trapezoids cover hundreds of meters, and enormous figures - a hummingbird, a spider, a monkey with a spiral tail - can only be seen complete from high above. Were they paths for ceremonial processions? Maps of underground water? Messages to the gods who looked down from mountain peaks? The builders left no written explanation, only these massive geoglyphs that have survived two thousand years of wind and sun.

sources.title: Serra da Capivara Rock Art
sources.author: Paleolithic inhabitants
sources.excerpt: These ancient paintings depict hunting scenes, ritual dances, and daily life of early inhabitants. The rock shelters contain over 30,000 pictographs showing human figures, animals, and geometric patterns spanning thousands of years.
sources.longExcerpt: These ancient paintings depict hunting scenes, ritual dances, and daily life of early inhabitants. The rock shelters contain over 30,000 pictographs showing human figures, animals, and geometric patterns spanning thousands of years. The Serra da Capivara National Park in Brazil contains one of the largest collections of prehistoric art in the Americas, providing insight into the lives of hunter-gatherers who inhabited the region over 10,000 years ago.

sources.title: Monte Alegre Cave Paintings
sources.author: Paleoindian artists
sources.excerpt: The cave walls show red and yellow paintings of human hands, animals, and geometric designs. These are among the oldest known artworks in South America, created by the first peoples to arrive in the Amazon basin.
sources.longExcerpt: The cave walls show red and yellow paintings of human hands, animals, and geometric designs. These are among the oldest known artworks in South America, created by the first peoples to arrive in the Amazon basin. Dating to approximately 11,000 years ago, these paintings in the Brazilian Amazon represent some of the earliest evidence of symbolic expression in the Americas.

sources.title: Chinchorro Mummification Practices
sources.author: Chinchorro culture
sources.excerpt: The Chinchorro people practiced artificial mummification, removing organs and skin, then reconstructing the body with clay and reeds. This process preserved their dead for the journey to the afterlife, showing sophisticated understanding of preservation techniques.
sources.longExcerpt: The Chinchorro people practiced artificial mummification, removing organs and skin, then reconstructing the body with clay and reeds. This process preserved their dead for the journey to the afterlife, showing sophisticated understanding of preservation techniques. These mummies from the Atacama Desert of Chile and Peru represent the world's oldest known artificial mummification, predating Egyptian mummies by thousands of years.
